hints: Filling a water cell joins whichever islands touch it. What would you need to know about a water cell to compute the result instantly?
The sizes of the distinct islands around it - distinct being the important word, since two of its neighbours can belong to the same island.
So label every island once, recording each label's size. Then each water cell is answered by looking at its four neighbours' labels.
Collect the neighbours' labels into a set before adding up their sizes, or an island touching the cell twice is counted twice. And remember the case where there is no water at all.
